## micromatch.diff.we-reject-UnterminatedBrace
# A `{` that never closes (30 rows)

## micromatch.diff.we-reject-UnterminatedClass
# A `[` that never closes (12 rows)
# globstar reads classes by POSIX's rules (GLOB_SPEC §8.5): a `]` first in the
# list is literal, and a class cannot hold `/`, so a `[` with no closing `]`
# after that is a parse error. The library accepts the pattern, as literal
# text or with the class crossing `/`; its answer is the row's comment.
# micromatch: match  [test/api.isMatch.js:226]
foo[/]bar	foo/bar	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/api.isMatch.js:355]
aaa[/]bbb	aaa/bbb	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/bash.js:165]
[]	a	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/bash.js:166]
[abc	[	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
[	[	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
[*	[abc	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/minimatch.js:37]  (and 1 more path)
[!a*	[!ab	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/special-characters.js:51]
[\\/]	\	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/special-characters.js:52]  (and 2 more paths)
[\\/]+	\	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.trailing-slash
# A trailing `/` (9 rows)
# A trailing `/` ends in an empty name: `a/*` matches `a/`, `a` does not match
# `a/` (GLOB_SPEC §9.5, §14.2). The library ignores a trailing `/`, or needs
# one on both sides.
# micromatch: no-match  [test/api.isMatch.js:396]
*/*	ab/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
a*b/*	a*b/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
a*?/*	a*b/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/stars.js:250]
*/*	a/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/stars.js:259]
a/*	a/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/stars.js:297]
a/**/*	a/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/stars.js:306]
a/**/**/*	a/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/stars.js:315]
a/**/**/**/*	a/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/stars.js:356]
**/*	foo/bar/	match	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.backslash
# A backslash in the pattern (8 rows)
# `\X` is the literal `X` for every `X` (GLOB_SPEC §4.1), inside classes too,
# and a path is never unescaped. The library gives some escapes another
# meaning (`\b`, `\w`), keeps the backslash, or unescapes the path.
# micromatch: no-match  [test/bash.js:70]
a[\b]c	abc	match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/bash.js:178]
f\oo	f\oo	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/extglobs-minimatch.js:638]
a\\z	a\\z	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/extglobs-minimatch.js:934]
\a\b\c	abc	match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/extglobs.js:606]
a\b	a\b	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/extglobs.js:617]
a\b	ab	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
a\*b/*	a*b/	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/minimatch.js:37]

## micromatch.diff.dot-segment
# A `.` or `..` segment (4 rows)
# `.` and `..` are plain names in a path and in a pattern (GLOB_SPEC §3.1);
# normalize paths first. The library strips a leading `./`, or never lets a
# wildcard match `.` or `..`.
# micromatch: match  [test/api.isMatch.js:117]
./*	ab	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/api.isMatch.js:119]
./*/	ab/	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
a/.*/b	a/./b	match	dot=false
# micromatch: no-match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
a/.*/b	a/../b	match	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.quoted-text
# Quotes in the pattern (4 rows)
# picomatch and micromatch read text in quotes as literal and drop the quotes,
# as a shell would. globstar has no quoting: a quote is a plain character
# (GLOB_SPEC §2).
# micromatch: match  [test/bash.js:36]
"***"	***	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/bash.js:38]
"*"*	*	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/bash.js:38]
"*"*	**	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/bash.js:38]
"*"*	*foo	no-match	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.we-reject-TrailingBackslash
# A pattern ending in `\` (3 rows)
# A `\` at the end escapes nothing and is refused (GLOB_SPEC §4.1); the
# library drops it or keeps it as a literal backslash.
# micromatch: no-match  [test/bash.js:115]  (and 1 more path)
\		err:TrailingBackslash	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/bash.js:121]
[A-Z]+/\	XXX/\	err:TrailingBackslash	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.brace-range
# A `{a..z}` range (3 rows)
# A `{1..3}` or `{a..c}` brace is a range to expand for the library. globstar
# has no ranges: the brace holds one literal branch, so it is literal text
# (GLOB_SPEC §6.1).
# micromatch: match  [test/braces.js:62]
a/{a..c}	a/a	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/braces.js:63]
a/{a..c}	a/b	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/braces.js:64]
a/{a..c}	a/c	no-match	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.dotfile
# A name starting with `.` (3 rows)
# Under `dot=false` no wildcard starts a name with `.` (GLOB_SPEC §3.1); under
# `dot=true` any does. The library draws this line elsewhere for some
# wildcards and positions.
# micromatch: match  [test/braces.js:87]
a{a,b/}*.txt	ab/.txt	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
[^a-c]*	.x	no-match	dot=false
# micromatch: match  [test/minimatch.js:37]
[^a-c]*	.y	no-match	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.class-or-literal
# A class matching its own text (1 row)
# picomatch and micromatch let a bracket expression match either one of its
# characters or its own literal text, so `*[1]` matches `copy [1]`. A class
# matches one character (GLOB_SPEC §8).
# micromatch: match  [test/micromatch.js:83]
a [b] c	a [b] c	no-match	dot=false

## micromatch.diff.we-reject-EscapedSeparator
# An escaped separator (1 row)
# `\/` is refused: a separator has no literal form (GLOB_SPEC §4.2). The
# library reads it as a plain `/`.
# micromatch: match  [test/special-characters.js:80]
D:\/\/*	D://foo	err:EscapedSeparator	dot=false
